title: Topboy
intro: Topboy begins with domination but develops a more practical argument about protecting the ability to make things and choose companions. Its adversary depends on publicity and pleasing others; the speaker wants recognition without that dependence. Genuine friends remain a source of happiness, so walking alone is not the entire ideal. Wings and a safe turn caution into preservation of future freedom. The return to the opening boasts also keeps the contradiction alive: a song warning against attention's power still enjoys demonstrating who stands above whom.
reading: Public superiority versus freedom from publicity; selective friendship and protecting future capacity.

revisions.31-n2: Selling a persona is followed immediately by fear of being forgotten. The accusation is not simply that an image is constructed—this song plainly constructs one too—but that the other person has become dependent on keeping it in circulation. Pleasing everyone then appears as the work required to prevent disappearance. The boastful speaker wants to distinguish his own authority from that dependency, though his need to compare himself keeps the distinction under strain.
revisions.editorial-31-audience-spit: The crowd supplies the opponent's humiliation while the speaker occupies the centre. In 'Throat', an audience similarly watched a performer suffer, but the vulnerable person was the speaker. Read alongside that song, this boast shows how easily spectatorship becomes a weapon when its target changes. The album does not offer one consistent position outside the cruelty of public attention; its voices can both suffer and enlist it.
revisions.editorial-31-brothers-well: Happiness at his brothers' success interrupts the need to surpass an opponent. Here someone else's flourishing is not a threat. That moment prepares the warning against calling everyone a brother: the label matters because genuine mutual regard is valuable. The song is distinguishing chosen care from indiscriminate affiliation, rather than arguing that dependence on any other person is inherently degrading.
revisions.editorial-31-heaven-choice: Heaven's will is followed by equal effort, no free reward and a decision left to the listener. The lines distribute control instead of settling on either fate or total self-sufficiency. One cannot guarantee outcomes, but can still choose where to put work and whom to trust. That practical mixture is more useful to the song's later advice than treating the heaven line as a complete philosophy of resignation.
revisions.editorial-31-wings: The wings are to be protected before the opportunity to fly arrives; the ideas are stored before they can be taken or exploited. These are images of preserving capacity, not just hiding from people. The final claim that school does not teach this makes the verse into an alternative lesson about creative and social survival. Its horizon extends beyond winning the present argument to remaining able to act later.
